newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CLT shareholders clear CLT-UFA merger.
newsitem.headline: CLT shareholders clear CLT-UFA merger.

text.p: Shareholders of Luxembourg broadcaster Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) on Monday gave the final go-ahead for the merger of CLT with Ufa, the television unit of German media group Bertelsmann.
"This is the final final final step," CLT-UFA spokesman Nikolaus Formanek told Reuters on Monday.

Bertelsmann and Audiofina signed an agreement to merge their audiovisual units in July, but the deal has taken a long time to get cleared by the boards and shareholders of the complex control structure above CLT.
On Tuesday, the new group will present itself to the press for the first time, at a news conference chaired by its two executive officers: CLT's Remy Sautter and UFA's Rolf Schmidt-Holtz.

The company will be managed jointly and equally by the two CEO's, with Sautter responsible for all non-German speaking television operations of CLT-UFA and radio and Schmidt-Holtz for German speaking television and international audiovisual rights.
Under the agreement, Audiofina and Bertelsmann will each hold 49 percent in CLT-UFA. Details of the full shareholder structure will be presented at Tuesday's news conference.
Audiofina is indirectly controlled by Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL). French Havas has a minority stake.
CLT-UFA will have its headquarters in Luxembourg, where the group's staff operations and main operations will be based.
The company gave up its ambitions in digital pay television in September, but remains one of Europe's top players in free, advertising-funded television.
